title: WorkOrder
description: The orchestrator → worker envelope (pure-skill architecture v1.0). Compiled by skills/tech-lead/scripts/compile-order.mjs, validated by validate-envelope.mjs before any worker dispatch. A worker depends only on this envelope — never on filesystem topology, run-state format, board schema, or another worker. Path: .shapeup/<slug>/orders/r<N>-a<M>.json (or <slug>/orders/<operation>.json for non-attempt work). Every record type and payload field is DEFINED CENTRALLY in domain.schema.json ($defs + x-payload-by-worker) — this file only shapes the envelope; it never re-defines a domain entity.

order_id.description: "<slug>/r<N>-a<M>" for build attempts, "<slug>/<operation>[-r<N>]" otherwise. Identifies a dispatch WITHIN a run — it repeats across runs of the same slug, which is why run_id exists.

run_id.description: OPTIONAL (v1.8) — the run this dispatch belongs to, stamped by compile-order.mjs from the receipt (skills/tech-lead/scripts/lib/run-id.mjs). The join key the analysis plane groups on: order_id alone collides across runs of the same slug, so without this no record the pipeline writes can be attributed to a run. Absent when no readable receipt exists (a standalone dispatch in a workspace with no open run) — never invented, and never required, because an analytic field must not be able to block a build.

compiled_at.description: OPTIONAL (v1.8) — ISO timestamp of compilation. The dispatch record's own time dimension: WorkResult carries none, and the journal's timings exist only on the workflow lane, so without this a dispatch on the prose lane is timeless.
